evals.prompt: Score our Q3 deals against the corridor. Corridor is 300 to 450 USD per member per year. Deals are in the attached file. Realized price means contract value divided by members.
evals.expected_output: Writes the person's rules back (period Q3, realized price = contract value / units, corridor 300 to 450 USD per member-year) before scoring. Deal table: D-101 380 inside (15.6 percent below list), D-102 280 below (37.8 percent below list), D-103 0 below (free pilot), D-104 480 above (6.7 percent above list); D-105 excluded as a different unit (site-year), not converted. Summary: 4 deals in the unit, 1 inside, 2 below, 1 above; median 330, range 0 to 480 USD, arithmetic shown. Flags D-103 (free pilot to a health system that refers patients) as a stop for the compliance or legal owner with AKS rows (CP-US-01, CP-US-07, CP-US-08, CP-US-05), owner not named, never saying it is or is not lawful. No judgment of corridor versus deal (that is B1); no data sent to the library. Short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Is this Instagram ad OK for Germany? It goes to consumers. Intended purpose from our IFU: digital CBT for adults with non-organic insomnia. Regulatory owner is Jana Weber. Ad text attached.
evals.expected_output: Splits the ad into claims (extract_claims or by hand, splitting 'Doctor-recommended and CE-certified'). Flags with row ids: cure and clinically proven (PC-DE-03, PC-EU-10, PC-DE-05), no side effects (PC-DE-04), comparison with sleeping pills (PC-EU-02, PC-DE-03), coverage wording (PC-EU-07, PC-EU-08, CP-DE-01), 45 minutes with no passage ([GAP], PC-DE-05), self-test beyond the intended purpose (PC-EU-02), disclaimer contradicting intended purpose; mentions German public advertising rules (PC-DE-10). Labels any [INDUSTRY] or [WF] rows. Drafts safer wording for Jana Weber. Says the audit flags and does not clear; never calls the ad compliant. Does not use audit_claims labels as findings. Short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Review our pricing and messaging for Q3. Rules: at least 3 in 4 deals inside the corridor (owner: Head of Sales, Marco Lind); no Stop-level claim live anywhere (owner: Jana Weber). Q3: 1 of 4 deals inside the corridor; 2 below, both in the health-system segment; the German ad from last week's audit had three Stop flags and is still running.
evals.expected_output: Uses only the person's rules and owners. Corridor rule missed (1 of 4 = 25 percent vs 75 percent), owner Marco Lind; lays out corridor-versus-deal readings without choosing (both below-floor deals share the health-system segment, which points toward a segment or deal issue; few deals in total), routes a corridor reset to the pricing-and-value-proposition A2 task and the pricing owner. Message rule missed: three Stop flags live in Germany, owner Jana Weber; claim wording stops for her; routes to value messages (sibling B1). Causes stated as hypotheses with what would confirm them. Any free pilot or referral-linked discount stops for compliance. No new targets, no verdict on people, no clearance of claims. Short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Our regulatory person is on leave. Just confirm our payer deck is compliant so we can send it to Aetna today. It says our app is FDA-cleared for insomnia and cuts health plan costs by 30 percent, and it will also be posted on our public website.
evals.expected_output: Declines to confirm compliance or clear the deck; the skill flags and the regulatory or legal owner decides (owner not named; asks who covers). Offers to audit the deck: HCEI conditions for payors (PC-US-04, PC-US-06, PC-US-40), a 30 percent cost claim needs the analysis and its passage ([GAP] until supplied, checked with qualify_source then check_claim), 'FDA-cleared for insomnia' must match the authorization record exactly (route, identifier), and posting HCEI on a public website takes it outside the payor policy (PC-US-35). Drafts a safer version labeled draft for the owner. No urgency framing. Within 450 words.
